name: Lumineers / no-prep veneers

lead: No-prep veneers are ultra-thin porcelain shells intended to need little or no filing of the natural tooth. Lumineers is a well-known brand name.
They are used for discolouration, shape and enamel defects.

paras: A thin porcelain layer is bonded to etched enamel, which is why less tooth reduction may be needed.
Veneers in general can chip, crack, leak or discolour, and can cause sensitivity and decay. One study cited in an encyclopedia article reported half of veneers unsatisfactory after 10 years.

lead: No-prep veneers are ultra-thin porcelain veneers that require little or no reduction of natural tooth structure; Lumineers is a commercial brand commonly associated with the category. A general encyclopedia article on veneers describes non-prep veneers in this way but flags the claim as needing a better source.[1]

Dental sources describe conventional porcelain veneers as typically lasting 10 to 30 years, with preparation that, if done by an inexperienced dentist, can remove a significant share of tooth surface.[1] Proponents of the minimal-grinding approach emphasise preservation of enamel.
infobox: Thin porcelain veneer, minimal or no tooth reduction

paras: Veneers are thin layers placed over the tooth surface, mainly for appearance, and are indicated for discolouration, malformation, enamel defects, fluorosis, fractures, wear and shape changes.[1] Porcelain veneers are made indirectly and in many cases need minimal or no preparation.[1]

Veneers were invented in 1928 by California dentist Charles Pincus for a film shoot. Etching of enamel was introduced by Michael Buonocore in 1959, and in 1982 Simonsen and Calamia showed porcelain could be etched with hydrofluoric acid to enable durable bonding.[1]

Contraindications listed for veneers include poor oral hygiene, uncontrolled gum disease, high cavity rate, parafunction and absent enamel.[1] Sensitivity and decay can occur even when the procedure is done properly, and one cited study found 50% of veneers displaced, retreated or unsatisfactory after 10 years.[1]
No studies found in the sources reviewed for this article that evaluate no-prep veneers specifically.

timeline.event: Charles Pincus creates veneers for film actors.[1]
Simonsen and Calamia show porcelain can be etched for bonding.[1]
